utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm sorry for the delay because of the technical problems as well as the overtime for this morning's case. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Mr. President. And this witness will not be asking for any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. Good afternoon. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could please tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: M-i-r-k-o-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mirkovic, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long have you lived in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: 47 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to focus you right into the point in time in question in this particular trial, July 1995. Could you please tell us what you were doing in Bratunac at that point in time, what job did you hold.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time the managing director of the Rad utilities company from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what is the Rad utilities company.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: The utilities company in Bratunac deals with the production and distribution of water with cleaning the town, maintaining the town parks, sewage system. These are the main activities, although we have had other activities as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sanitation being one of them, also known as asanacija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long did you work for the Rad company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: 30 years, up to 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you hold --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: So it's seven years less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you hold the position as managing director?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Up to 1995, I'd had three terms, that is 12 years, as managing director.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecution. Let me repeat the question. Did you give a statement to the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. In Banja Luka, in 2000.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you had an opportunity to look at that statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before we talk about the events and we talk about some of the issues or some of the matters you discussed in Banja Luka, could you please tell us whether the dates that are in your statement are correct, to your understanding.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a particular explanation as to why perhaps the dates are not correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I think the main reason is that Mr. Ruez suggested these dates to me and I simply agreed to them. Later on when I read my statement, I realised that these dates were not right. I wouldn't like to mention any dates. I wouldn't like to be held to that, because I don't remember the dates anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But there were some times in your statement, as I understand, where you seem to be under the impression that a certain event occurred at a particular time.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: These dates are dates that were suggested to me, and I simply agreed to them. As I said, I don't really want to discuss dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, do you recall if you were given any tasks on the day that Srebrenica fell, and that day is July 11, 1995? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall being given any assignments or being given any orders with respect to asanacija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 11th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in general, the 11th, the 12th, the 13th, those dates, since you don't know the exact dates, do you recall at least incidents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked you whether you're referring to the 11th. I don't remember the date, but I did get specific tasks to carry out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. May I ask you: Who gave you those tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: These tasks or orders were given to me by Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you know Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: That was the first time I had met him personally, but I had seen him in Bratunac one or two times before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of him, his reputation, the position he held, sort of things that he was involved in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I knew he was a high-ranking officer of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which sector, which organ, of the VRS he was in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, where was it that you met Colonel Beara or how is it that he gave you certain orders with respect to asanacija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I was told to come to the SDS offices in Bratunac, and that's what I did. On my arrival at the SDS offices, I saw two military policemen in front of the door. I introduced myself to them and told them that I was supposed to see Colonel Beara at his invitation. They let me go in, into the premises of the SDS. And that was the office of the then-president of the SDS, Miroslav Deronjic. I found Colonel Beara there and two other officers whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. And I want to go step by step so we don't miss any details. Where were you when you were contacted to meet Colonel Beara at the SDS office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: At that point of time, I was in my office in the utilities company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the utilities company in relation to the SDS office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I think about 150 metres away, downstream along the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall about what time it was when you were informed to meet Colonel Beara at the SDS office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what time it was, but it was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the lighting conditions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: It was evening, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean in a sense that it was dark, getting dark?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the two, dark dark or just about to go dark?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: It was just beginning to get dark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know how it -- when you received the notice, would you please tell us - if you recall - who it was that gave you that notice, that placed the phone call? Was it Beara himself or someone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I was informed by telephone that I was to report to the SDS offices and that Colonel Beara was waiting for me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to the SDS office, you indicated that you went in to Mr. Deronjic's office, where you found Colonel Beara and two officers. Was Mr. Deronjic there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- did you recognise the two other officers that were with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they introduce themselves to you to tell you whether they were from the Main Staff, the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they weren't. I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it one of them was not Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Momir Nikolic wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could please describe to us what exactly happened at that meeting at the SDS office with Colonel Beara and the two officers that were with him with the two military police standing outside the door.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in the office, I told the colonel, Colonel Beara: "Here I am. My name is Dragan Mirkovic. I am the managing director of the utilities company. You asked to see me." He said: "Take a seat." I sat down. He offered me a drink. There was a bottle of whiskey in front of him and a glass. I said I didn't drink. Then he asked me what kind of machinery we had at the utilities company and how many men I had. I told him that we had a small Skip backhoe excavator and that I could ask for as many men as I needed from the military department. These were unfit for military service, and it all depended on the need at the time. That's why the numbers varied. I told him I could check exactly how many men we had. And I also said that we had two trucks at the utilities company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. You said that you could get men from the military department.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was that the Workers' Battalion or are you referring to the workers' unit? What exactly are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: This was a unit consisting of men unfit for military service, who were mobilised to carry out a work obligation in the utilities company. And they did the work that had previously been done by employees of the company who had now been mobilised into the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you informed Colonel Beara about the resources that were available and the men that you could get a hold of for any work that needed to be done, what was his response?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: He said to me: "You'll get these men and these machines ready. You will be informed when to set out towards Milici. You have to go to the bauxite mine there." I asked him why, what for? And he told me: "There will be a lot of dead who have to be buried." I asked him: "Colonel, is this all right for us to do this in Milici? And I don't have the proper machinery, I don't have enough men for this kind of work." They asked whether Mr. Rajko Dukic would have this done up there. He then swore at me. He cursed Rajko Dukic. He said: "Go outside. Get out. And you will receive orders what to do next." And that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you. When he said there would be a lot of dead, did he say whether they would be Serb or Muslim or both, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. He didn't say whether they were Serbs or Muslims. He just said there will be a lot of dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, first of all please explain to us how is it that Colonel Beara, who is with the Main Staff, giving you an order to do something when you are not in the military and you are instead with an enterprise, utilities company, which is a municipal enterprise as I understand it, of Bratunac. Would you please tell us how is it that he could be giving you an order.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I asked myself, why and how he could be issuing orders to me, as the managing director of the utilities company. Had I then been the komandir of the civilian protection, I would have understood his issuing me orders for asanacija, or sanitisation of the terrain. But as I was the managing director of the utilities company and I had nothing to do with the civilian protection, I thought, well, this was simply because we had the machinery, which we would give at the request of Ljupko Ilic for asanacija, or sanitisation of the terrain. We would supply not only the machinery but also a certain number of men when they were needed. I didn't dare refuse the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, it was wartime. I was a civilian. A colonel was issuing orders to me. Well, it's not that easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said that there was a bottle of whiskey and a glass. Could you tell us whether you had noticed if Colonel Beara had been consuming any whiskey himself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Beara was drinking whiskey at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was he sober and just having a friendly drink, or did he appear to be more in -- slightly intoxicated, intoxicated? How would you describe his appearance, if you can?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think the colonel was tipsy. I couldn't say he was really drunk, but he was under the influence of alcohol. Because he wouldn't have sworn at Mr. Rajko Dukic and me that way had he been sober.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So I take it you left as you were ordered. What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I returned to my office, and from my office I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you contacted again, as he indicated that he would be getting a hold of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when it was that you were contacted and where you were at the time you were contacted.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I was contacted after midnight. It was long after midnight, perhaps 2.00, 2.30, or 3.00 a.m. I was at home. I received a phone call and was told to report again to the SDS offices and that there I would be told what I was to do the next day. I got ready and went there. I found two guards, that is two policemen, at the door and Colonel Beara, who was in the SDS office or Miroslav Deronjic's office alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice whether Mr. Deronjic was in or about the area when you went there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, I didn't see Mr. Deronjic at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So could you please tell us what happened when you got there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Beara told me -- well, he offered me some whiskey again and I refused. It wasn't even dawn yet. And he said to me: "You will now take a vehicle. You will find the location where the dead are to be buried." I refused this. I said: "Who am I to look for a location for a burial site?" He said: "Well, then, you will take this military policeman with you who is at the door and he will show you where the site is." I left the office and one of those two military policemen went with me. We got in a vehicle. We went to Glogova. We turned off the main road on to the so-called old Kravica road, and we went some 100 or 150 metres down the road, and he said: "This is the site." Then we went back to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you now. The MP, the military police officer that escorted you to that location, did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other MP that was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's some water there, too, if you need to drink. Do you know whether they were from the Bratunac Brigade, these two MPs that were guarding or securing Colonel Beara at the SDS office on that particular early morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, they weren't from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what about the vehicle that took you and the military police officer? Was that your vehicle? Their vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: The military policeman did the driving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that vehicle belonging to - if you know - the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you returned, could you please tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. The next morning, did you go back to the site in Glogova where you had been ordered by Colonel Beara to dig?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: That morning, just like all other mornings, I went to work as usual, to my company. I made a schedule of assignments, and I said who was to do what. We went to the site. The people who had a work obligation with the utilities company at the time were transported there in two trucks, which was owned by the utilities company. One of the two trucks in the meantime broke down, so we sent it back. We didn't take the backhoe excavator Skip with us then, because that machine was not suitable for the work that colonel asked to be done. But instead, he sent an ULT machine, a loader, in order to dig out the mass grave with that machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here for a second. Now, this particular ULT, do you know where it was from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: When the machine came to Glogova, I saw that it was an ULT owned by the brick factory from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you recall who was operating the ULT on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, the machine was operated by Rade Djurkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how he got there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Beara asked me in the SDS premises whether I had that machine in my utilities company, the backhoe Skip excavator, and he asked me who operated the machine. I told him it was Rade Djurkovic. He asked me where the man was at the time. I told him he was mobilised, he was a soldier. He told me, "All right, in that case, I'll take care of it." The following day, Rade was already there at the site with the machine. I simply marked what I had been told to mark, that is to say the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us how large of a site you had been asked to mark.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a fairly large area. And precisely because it was large, the ULT machine, which as we know is a loader and not an excavator, was not suitable. So I informed Colonel Beara, I don't know how, but I informed him that I couldn't do the work with the ULT, and that for a job of that nature we needed a large excavator. He said that a large excavator would arrive and that he would ask for it from the Zvornik Brigade. In late afternoon, the machine arrived from the direction of Kravica. It arrived in Glogova on a tractor. The tractor went back to Kravica, whereas the machine remained at the Glogova site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that -- when you say "on a tractor," the tractor was pulling a platform and this excavating machine was on top of the platform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was towed. The machine was towed. It was a truck that towed the platform, and the excavator sat on the platform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you said it arrived late afternoon. Again, do you know what time it was or could you tell us the lighting conditions at -- you know, when this machine came --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the evening. There was still light, but it was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know whether that machine was put to work on that particular -- when it arrived, on that particular evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us whether that machine arrived with an operator.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it there was or there were operators for that particular piece of machine at the site?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was there another individual that was operating any of the machines that you recall, if you recall? If not, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Rade Djurkovic, Simic --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be Krsto Simic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Krsto Simic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, could you tell us, if you recall, how long, how many days, this operation took, the digging itself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Once the machine arrived from Zvornik, as Colonel Beara had said, it was put to use and it was operated as long as there was light. ULT was parked. It wasn't used at the time, because it wasn't suitable. The other machine was the only one that was used. As soon as it became dark, we left the area. I think -- I don't know how many people, two, three, or five, in uniforms remained to guard the machine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those in uniform, were they from the Bratunac Brigade, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know any of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You didn't recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether they were from any particular unit, other than the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to speak with any of them, to ask them any questions, where they might have come from, who had sent them, what they were doing there, how long they were there, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Colonel Blagojevic come to that site while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you participate at all in the filling up of those graves -- or were you involved, I should say? Did those graves -- were those graves that were dug up, were they ultimately filled with bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "Da," that means yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, ask your question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did -- did you participate, did you participate, in the filling up of those graves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I was in charge of the digging of the graves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you watch the graves being filled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for a certain amount of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who was filling them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: The trucks brought them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Where were the trucks from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: There had been requisitioned trucks in Milici, Zvornik, Vlasenica, there was one truck from the utilities company. But mostly Zvornik, Milici, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the drivers were from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the driver -- who was driving the truck from the utility company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Milivoje Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's from Bratunac, I take it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know how many days it took to fill the graves and to cover the bodies up, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: From the time Colonel Beara issued an order to me, people from the utilities company and myself stayed there for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were you there the entire time or were you coming and going?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there the entire time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would you go back -- when you were not there, would you go back to your office in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you went home at night, to your home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know whether Colonel Beara ever showed up at those sites while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he did not or you're not sure? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: While I was there, he did not show up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You did not see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk to you about another -- about an incident that occurred at the Kravica warehouse. Did you ever hear about that incident?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Not to the warehouse itself, but I was there on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, could you please tell us -- well, do you know -- you said that you weren't familiar with dates, but you recall going to that area. So please tell us: When you went there, what if anything did you notice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I went from Glogova to Konjevic Polje, because a unit from the utilities company was out there on the field. There were a couple of people there who were collecting bodies with several people from the utilities company and the company's truck. They were collecting bodies of the people who had been killed. So I went to Konjevic Polje, too, to see what was going on, more out of curiosity. I saw in Kravica a site that I will never forget. I saw the killing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us exactly what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I saw one man taking five people who were entering the compound of the co-op Oka, co-op in Kravica. The man was in uniform and had an automatic rifle in his hands. And he ordered the five men to lie face down, and then he shot them in the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you try to stop this from happening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any reports to anyone with respect to these events?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any individuals that were committing these killings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you spoke to the Prosecution and you gave your statement back on 13 October 2002, I've noticed that you omitted this detail in your statement. Would you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a particular reason why you didn't tell Mr. Ruez about what you had witnessed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell that to the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I was afraid to tell about this to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to switch to another area, another place where there might have been or there were, in fact, killings. And that's the Vuk Karadzic school. Were you ever asked to go there for asanacija purposes to collect any bodies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: We were collecting bodies there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who informed you that you had to go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember who informed me, but a group of people from the utilities company was tasked with going there in a truck and collecting the dead bodies. We had heard the shooting around the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you yourself go there to see how many bodies there were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I was by the school only once, and I saw five or six corpses. However, after that the driver Cvjetinovic, Milivoje, informed me that there had been many more dead there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you ever tell Momir Nikolic anything about collecting those bodies and unloading them someplace?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just to be on the safe side perhaps we could go through what Mr. Nikolic said during his testimony when he was being questioned by Mr. McCloskey. And I have for the ELMO the appropriate pages. For the record, it's page 1771. And I'll be reading from line 7. I will go slowly. You won't need to read. This is all in English. But I will go slowly, step by step, and perhaps you can help us here. Mr. Nikolic is being asked, and this is from line 9: "All right, Mr. Nikolic, one other question on that topic. You told us you received information about 80 to 100 bodies from the school area in Bratunac from, I think, Dragan Mirkovic. Is that right?" And his answer is: "Yes, that's what I said." Did you give him any information about those bodies being at the school?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question, the next question, line 13: "Did you receive any information from him where those bodies were deposited?" And here is what Momir Nikolic stated under oath, line 15, page 1771: "Yes, Your Honours. Dragan Mirkovic also informed me that the killed Muslims killed in the night between the 13th and the 14th had been collected during the night and in the early morning of the 14th, and transferred into the surroundings of Glogova in an isolated place close to Avdagina Njiva" - I butchered the name - "and that they were just covered by earth and buried in that way, unloaded and covered by earth." Sir, did you ever tell this to Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He goes on. Question: "When you say 'unloaded,' did you receive information of how they were unloaded or how they were deposited?" Again, Momir Nikolic, line 23, page 1771, here is what he said under oath: "Yes. Dragan Mirkovic told me that representatives of the civilian authorities had asked for a truck from his company which was an FAP 13, a truck that can lift -- the back of which can be lifted and in that way the load deposited." Did you ever say any of this to Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question by Mr. McCloskey: "Were you provided information about the geographic descriptions of the area that they were unloaded in?" Momir Nikolic answer, line 4, 1772, again under oath says: "Yes, he," that being you, "he told me that this was done in an area which is about 1 kilometre away from this mass grave and that when you come to Av--" this village that you can see -- "you take a turn to the right. And after a certain distance, this was done where there was no settlement. In the border area of," this place. I'm paraphrasing because I can't pronounce the village. "He mentioned the village of Halilovici. I don't know where that village is situated, but I do know the road and where it leads to." Did you ever tell this to Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you, and I want to underscore that, had you told that to Nikolic and had you deposited, collected and deposited the bodies in a manner which Momir Nikolic described to the Trial Chamber under oath, would you be willing to tell us that here today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you ever go to Potocari during those days --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to conduct any asanacija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked to go to Srebrenica to conduct any asanacija?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it, when you were being questioned by Mr. Ruez in Banja Luka, the gentleman drew some maps and had you look at them. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact last night for the first time you pulled out of your briefcase copies of those maps which Mr. Ruez had drawn and had you mark and which you signed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact we looked at some of those exhibits. You don't have to go through your briefcase. But let me ask you -- let me just show you. I guess we can go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you what I was just handed by the Prosecutor prior to the commencement. We'll put it on the ELMO. And we can see from the ELMO that this has an ER number of 01068740. Sir, do you recognise your signature on this page?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could point where it would be. You have to look at -- we lost it. We seem to have a technical problem. But we can move along. In looking at that map, if you could just look at it. If you could just look at it. That's your signature on the right-hand corner, right-hand bottom corner. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there are some -- did you draw that or did you just make some markings on it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez drew it and he also put in markings on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there seem to be some dates there. Is that your handwriting or is that the handwriting of Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: This is not my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But I take it the dates that he placed there were based on the dates that you might have given him. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez drew these -- extracted these dates from me. He was the one who mentioned the dates. I was not ready, not prepared, for this. So I simply agreed to the dates he stated, and that's what he wrote down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But the location that we have, as we have the road of Konjevic Polje and where the locations of these -- of the X's and the little squares are and the circles, that would be correct as to where the graves are, correct, the ones that you assisted in digging?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, at some point in time did you go to the site with Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: To this site you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you -- let me -- let me -- let me go back. At some point did you meet Mr. Ruez again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you meet him in Banja Luka or was it in the field?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: The second time, it was in Bratunac -- or rather, in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So that would be at around this area that we have on the map, more or less?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, we don't have anything from the Prosecution with respect to this particular meeting, what might have transpired, what might you have said, what questions might have been asked, what information you might have provided. So could you please tell us first of all how it is that you met Mr. Ruez in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: The interpreter, what's his name? Can you help me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interpreter from the OTP, the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The one who was in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, in any event how was it that you met Ruez? That's my question. Were you contacted? Were you asked to meet him there? Did he show up one day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreter called me on the phone at home and told me -- or rather, he told my daughter, because I wasn't in, that he would call on the following day between 6.00 and 7.00, and that's what happened. He called me and he said: "We are setting out to Bratunac. We'll meet in Glogova in an hour or an hour and a half. Will you come there with your car?" And I said: "Yes, I will." I went there. They were waiting for me. It was -- well, there were a lot of SFOR soldiers around. There were people in white coats, probably from some sort of medical department or sanitisation department. And then we made the sketch. He then said to me: "Will you indicate here on the site where the graves were dug." And I showed this to him. Then he asked me: "Mr. Mirkovic, did you dig this grave which is about 6 or 7 metres long?" I said: "Probably. When all this was dug, this grave was dug also." You see, he said: "Mr. Nikolic forgot to steal these corpses and transfer them elsewhere. And here we found the corpses of 12 people who had been killed. They were tied two together with barbed wire and all shot in the forehead. Do you know anything about this?" And I said I didn't. "It's possible," he said, "that this was done by Mr. Lazar Ostojic and his soldiers." And he pointed with his hand. "That's where they were at the line, and these are probably people who surrendered to the soldiers of Lazar Ostojic or they were caught in the woods fleeing from Srebrenica. And these are the men who were killed." He said: "Are you sure you know nothing about this?" And I said: "No, I don't know anything about it." From there we went for me to show them a mass grave from 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I -- did Mr. Ruez show you any documentation or any proof as to why he thought Mr. Lazar Ostojic had committed those crimes, on what basis he was providing this information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't show me any documents. That's what he said to me, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Lazar Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was with the Bratunac Brigade, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked by Ruez that he had -- or you were told that he had documentation that the Bratunac Brigade military police were guarding the equipment there for that period of time up until, I believe, the 19th. Did you at any point in time notice anyone from the Bratunac Brigade military police guarding any of the equipment there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had seen members of the Bratunac Brigade military police or any of their officers there guarding the equipment or assisting in this enterprise, would you hide that from us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you know Mr. Blagojevic, do you know not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you know him since you were a child. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to school together. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're from the same generation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it when he became the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, you had opportunities to at least see each other, perhaps even have a coffee or a drink on a social occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say, Mr. Mirkovic, that Mr. Blagojevic is a friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you lie for your friend? Would you lie to protect Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: When I started testifying, I took an oath that I would speak only the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before taking that oath, I had warned you during the proofing session, had I not, that you could be facing charges of perjury if you failed to tell us the truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe it's time for the break. I don't believe I have any further questions, but if we're going to take the break I would like to sort of do a mental accounting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you insist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I thought it was the time, Your Honour, for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, do you have more questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to ask to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I will try to be very brief, but I need to put a few questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you to help me clarify some of your responses during the examination-in-chief. Could you please tell us since when you have known Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I've known Colonel Beara since -- well, actually two or three days before I met him, I saw him for the first time in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "when I met him," you're referring to the event you described?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were called to the SDS offices in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of meeting was it? Did somebody introduce Colonel Beara to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the office at the colonel's invitation, and I knew him by sight. He is a tall man. So I was able to recognise him by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We heard some testimony here yesterday from a protected witness who also spoke about this meeting. Can you recall whether anybody else attended the meeting. I am referring to members of the civilian authorities or the civilian protection, but please don't mention any names. If someone like that was present, just say yes or no if not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: When I was invited to the SDS offices, nobody else was present, except for Colonel Beara and the two officers I mentioned and whom I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this conversation you were told to go in the direction of the mine and the Milici municipality. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They said they expected quite a lot of dead without saying what kind of dead and who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in saying that at that time the mine in Milici was the best-equipped company, as far as machinery goes, excavators and so on, in the north-eastern part of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think you're correct in saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, since we speak the same language, can we just pause a little between question and answer so that the interpreters have time to interpret what we are saying. Thank you. Did you then think it was odd that he should be asking you, with the modest resources you had at your disposal, to go in the direction of the mine at Milici, which was so well equipped?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's why I asked the colonel: "Is it all right for us to do that up there and take the machinery from Bratunac?" And the machinery wasn't even suited for that kind of job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I would be correct in saying that this was illogical, because the equipment and the machinery belonging to the mine was superior to what you had at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's what he asked of me, to prepare the machinery I had at my disposal, to get it ready, and to go to Milici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You are the managing or you were the managing director of the utilities company for 20 -- for 12 years --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that this is a public company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you were funded from the budget of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the utilities company funded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Not from the budget, but from the sale of water and from the funds we received for refuse disposal. And the only thing that was funded from the budget was washing the streets and cleaning the parks. So this was a smaller part of the work that we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All public activities, such as maintaining public areas, public parks, burials if requested by the municipality were funded from the budget. And the rest was paid for by subscribers, came from your revenue. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the law on defence in these wartime conditions, who issued you with your orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean in time of war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In time of war.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: We were supposed to receive orders from the president of the Municipal Assembly and the president of the Executive Board. From various inspectors, utility, sanitary, building inspectors, depending on the job we had to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case you were not subordinated to the army, but you were to be coordinated -- your activities were to be coordinated with those of the army through the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also spoke about the arrival of a heavy-duty machine in Glogova from the direction of Kravica -- or rather, Konjevic Polje. And you mentioned the truck towing that machine. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what sort of vehicle this was, the vehicle towing the excavator? Can you tell us anything about its colour, make, and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: This towing truck, I think it was yellow. It was an FAP 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the platform on which the machine was, was it blue? Was it MAS make? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you allow for this possibility. It could have been blue. It could have been MAS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as for the make, I can't say anything about that. I didn't observe what make it was. I didn't look.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will now put to this witness a statement made by a protected witness, so I ask to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we are in open session, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to put these events in chronological sequence, if we can. As far as I was able to understand, after you saw this machine arriving you decided to go toward Konjevic Polje, and that's when you saw that incident in Kravica. Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not right away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was on that day -- just a moment. The machine arrived, it was digging, and I went to Konjevic Polje on the following day, not that day. It was on the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's very important to us. So the event in Kravica that you saw and described here occurred the day after this machine started operating in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether there was another incident, now that we mention the incident in Kravica, the execution, apart from the one you saw on that day? I'm talking about the supermarket in Kravica, to be more precise, or rather, the Kravica warehouse or the co-op in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened in Kravica and the surrounding area the day before I left for Konjevic Polje was that a truckload of corpses was brought to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to finish this area, do you know Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: From television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw him in Zvornik, in Bratunac in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "from television," did you -- are you referring to the reports from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no positive or negative reports about him outside the context of The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: It was from the trial at The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. If I could just have the Court's indulgence for one minute while I fix this podium. Cross-examined by Mr. Shin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- I'd like to begin by looking at the issue of the dates in your -- in the interview that you gave to Mr. Ruez, an issue you've already talked a little bit about today. Now, you stated today that you believe Mr. Ruez extracted the dates that were in your statement from you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I used the word "extracted," but that he led the conversation. He would give me the dates and I would confirm them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you would give him the dates and then he would confirm or he would give you the dates and you would confirm?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask -- I didn't object yesterday, but I would ask the gentleman to please listen to the answers before asking the next questions, because his answer was very -- very clear. And I don't want to confuse the witness anymore than he might be confused with respect to the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Shin, I think you have to rephrase your question because I also got confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'll be happy to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps I could rephrase it this way. You testified -- perhaps I can approach the issue in this way. You testified today that you did not know the date that Srebrenica fell. Is that correct? Sorry. I'm not sure if -- did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified today that you did not know -- let me put it more precisely. You did not know at the time of your interview with Mr. Ruez, you did not know the date that Srebrenica fell. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I talked with Mr. Ruez in Banja Luka, I didn't know at that time. Just a bit ago, you stated that I had mentioned that here, and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were being interviewed by Mr. Ruez, do you recall that you gave him some information -- you told him some things, on the basis of which he was able to suggest a date to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the questioning is going to go in that route, in fairness to the witness I think he needs to confront the witness and show him exactly what he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin, your question is too broad, you know. What is something, some information, which is too broad. You have to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'd be happy to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, do you recall that when you were being interviewed by Mr. Ruez, you told him that Colonel Beara had called for you to meet with him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your interview with Mr. Ruez, you told him about your meeting with Colonel Beara. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told Mr. Ruez that that meeting occurred on the day before the fall of Srebrenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, it was on the basis of that information that Mr. Ruez was able to suggest a date to you for that meeting. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to object. I mean, now we're reading into Ruez's mind. If he could point how it is that Mr. Ruez on that basis was suggesting dates, I have no objection. But I think that he's asking now to delve into Mr. Ruez state of mind as to what he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I believe that this question has no problem. But on the other hand, Mr. Shin, you have to give us some indications. For instance, the witness said that maybe two days of the fall of Srebrenica or one day after, you know, the fall of Srebrenica, then Mr. Ruez asked this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, what I'm seeking to do is explain that, or to show that the witness had told Mr. Ruez that the meeting with Mr. Beara occurred on the day before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And on that basis, certain dates had been placed on the events that occurred after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed with your question, but I don't know how the witness will answer that question. You may try your luck.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, it was after you told Mr. Ruez that your meeting with Colonel Beara was on the day before the fall of Srebrenica. It was after that that he suggested to you a date on which that interview took place -- I'm sorry, that meeting took place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that to Mr. Ruez because for me, as a civilian at the time, as someone who hadn't done the military service, the fall of Srebrenica was on the day when the buses and trailer trucks were driving away women, children, the elderly. So it is likely that this is what I said, that that was a day before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And it was only after you said that that -- that was on the day before the fall of Srebrenica, it was after that that Mr. Ruez suggested a date when that meeting had taken place, that meeting with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that, Mr. Mirkovic. You also said in your testimony, near the end of your testimony, that Mr. Ruez had gone with you to the Glogova site. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said -- I believe you -- you testified here that he said that this was possible that this had been the work of Mr. Lazar Ostojic and his men. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like to move now, Mr. Mirkovic, to the issue of your meeting with Colonel Beara, and that's the meeting where you raise the matter of Mr. Djurkovic, who was the operator for one of the machines. Now, you told Colonel Beara that Mr. Djurkovic was not available because he was mobilised. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that means that he was mobilised in the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where Mr. Djurkovic was at that time when you were having this meeting with Colonel Beara, in terms of where his work assignment was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was somewhere on the front lines, though, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. He indicated already. It's been asked and answered. He didn't know. Now it's suggesting a possibility where he might be. It was asked and answered. He got his answer; he didn't like the answer. Now he's trying to pin him in this front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there some reason in this objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified about the warehouse in Kravica today. I'd like to ask you a few questions about that. Can you tell us who first told you that you had to go to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember who told me that bodies need to be collected in Konjevic Polje and along the road. I couldn't go myself -- I didn't have to go myself. I could have just sent the driver with the truck and the men to collect the bodies; however, I wanted to see myself what was going on. And to see the corpses that needed to be collected. I wanted to see how many there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to the events at Kravica warehouse itself, but I'd like to return now first to this issue of who had first told you about this. Now, you had a chance to review the transcript of your interview with Mr. Ruez. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you read it prior to this testimony in the past few days. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did reviewing that help refresh your memory as to whether -- as to who had told you about the bodies in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the man. He was a man in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. This man in the uniform, did he speak to you in person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: In Glogova, at the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he -- sorry. I'll let -- if you could finish. I'm sorry I cut you off. I thought you were saying something else.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to say the green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that green camouflage uniform an army uniform, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for me as a civilian, all green uniforms were the same. To me, they were all camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask this person who he was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was an officer of any type?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what made you think that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Because he had an insignia on the pocket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the insignia he had on his pocket?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Probably indicating his rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what this person told you precisely?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: He told me to go with the truck and the people to collect the dead on the road between Kravica and Konjevic Polje and said that there were also some dead in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the dead in Kravica itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you about the dead in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing. He just said that there were some dead there, some people who had been killed in Konjevic Polje, and that their bodies needed to be collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you yourself went to Konjevic Polje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In a passenger vehicle, whereas I told the driver and the men to go to Konjevic Polje to collect that. One team had already been in Konjevic Polje. I had some food in my car, and I took the food to these people who had already been there. And then the truck and some additional people came there subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was your -- that team, was that one of your teams? Was it a team from the public utilities company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that team sent there in response to this conversation with this army -- with this officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they had been sent there previously?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was it that had instructed that that team go to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think that it was agreed with Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could return now to the site of Kravica. Do you recall what time it was that you got there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure what time it was exactly, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any bodies, apart from those five that you saw when you got there, those five that you testified about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were those bodies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: They were in front of the building of Oka, in Kravica. And the killing was before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear about that, the killing was before that in that it occurred before that? I'm not sure I understood that answer, not in English anyway. Let me try to put the question to you again. Did you see bodies at Kravica, apart from those five that you saw getting shot while you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these bodies, where were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the building of Oka in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many bodies were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say now. There was a pile of bodies. I couldn't tell you how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were there, were there people who were removing those bodies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: When I was there, nobody was moving the bodies. There were no people in uniform within the compound. There was the man whom I saw shoot these people, the five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the man that you saw shooting those people was outside of the compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else in that area outside the compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were people in uniforms, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people, approximately?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw some 10 to 15 within the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You just stated a minute ago that there were no people in uniform within the compound. Are you changing your answer or is this a clarification of your answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't mention that at all. Perhaps it was a misunderstanding. I didn't mention that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In that case if we can just clarify this. Your testimony is that "there were these 10 to 15 men within the compound."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these men were in uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these men were armed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these men doing, apart from the one man that you've told us about already?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Some were walking about. Some were just standing. Some were close to this site where the other man killed those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any machinery there when you were at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a bus in front of the warehouse at Kravica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the Kravica building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in front of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the night that you had your meetings with Colonel Beara, did you see any buses in Bratunac town that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I did see them one night, but I don't know. There were two or three buses in front of the municipal building. But I couldn't tell you what night it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether that was before or after the night when you had your meetings with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think it was that night when I had the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who was inside those buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: There were many women, children, men, especially the elderly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if the buses were parked there? Was the engine running?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether the engine was running, but the buses were parked in front of the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall either that evening, or maybe a couple days before, a couple days after, meeting Mr. Davidovic in his office in the municipal building at about 7.00 in the evening, 7.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that before or after that evening or was it that evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: That evening when there were buses there, I remember that Mr. Davidovic and I brought water to the people, women and children, who asked for it. I had some jerrycans at my office and I brought them there, poured water into them, and then we distributed that in the buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that evening or the following morning that there had been many more buses and trucks full of people in Bratunac town that night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that evening. What I saw ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear about it the following day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN MIRKOVIC
